sections.html:
You record Cherokee County land documents with the Register of Deeds in Murphy (75 Peachtree Street, Suite 126-A, phone 828-837-2613), open for land records from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Surveys, UCC statements, soldier discharges and notary certifications are handled there too, along with local vital records.

Cherokee County has roughly 30,830 residents and 19,158 housing units, with 83.7% owner-occupied. Between 2020 and 2024 the middle owned home was worth $232,300, and homeowners with a loan paid a median $1,242 each month. Prices are moderate, so a seller's stamp tax stays small relative to typical equity.

Recording costs $26 for a deed of up to fifteen pages. A deed of trust costs $64 for up to thirty-five. Past those limits, each added page is $4.

Fees posted at the Murphy counter
ServiceCharge

Plats filed after October 1991 must be clear mylar, sized 18 by 24, 21 by 30 or 24 by 36 inches. The recording amounts track the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10, and a cancellation of a deed of trust is recorded without charge.

The local stamp is $2 for each $1,000 of the price, equal to the statutory $1.00 per $500. By G.S. 105-228.30 the seller owes it, and it must reach the register ahead of filing. One half stays in the county's general fund, and Raleigh receives the rest.

Points a seller should know:

  • The stamp shows up among the seller's charges at closing.
  • Each $500 of price is taxed, and a partial $500 rounds up.
  • Under G.S. 47-18, an option, a contract to convey or a lease over three years binds later purchasers and lien creditors only after registration in the land's county.

sections.h2: Looking up tax and deed information
sections.html:
The county's interactive tax viewer displays tax amounts from 2008 forward. It refreshes each morning at 6 a.m., so a payment appears the next day. It was compiled for county use from recorded deeds and plats, so verify anything important against the public record.

When a value, parcel record or deed looks wrong, call the Cherokee County Appraisal Office at 828-835-3296. The recorded original is kept in Murphy, and certified copies of it are available there.

sections.h2: Tax relief that changes when you sell
sections.html:
Three groups of owners can ask the county assessor for relief: seniors, disabled owners and owners with a disabled-veteran designation. For 2026, a senior or disabled owner earning $38,800 or less may exclude the greater of $25,000 or half of appraised value. The disabled veteran exclusion covers the first $45,000 and has no age or income limit. File form AV-9 by June 1 before the tax year. The statutes are G.S. 105-277.1 and G.S. 105-277.1C.

Already getting one of these benefits? Ask the Appraisal Office how a sale affects it before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: How a deed gets from closing table to the record
sections.html:
Your attorney normally runs this sequence. The deed is drafted and signed by every owner on title. The seller's stamp tax is figured from the purchase price and held back from the proceeds. The recording fee is added, and the package reaches the Murphy office before 4:30 p.m. After recording, the register keeps the original, and the new owner can order a certified copy at $5 for page one and $2 for each page after.

If you transfer property without a closing attorney, bring the signed original, payment for the fee and stamps, and a return address. Staff will not fix drafting errors, so settle any wording questions before you arrive. Aim to arrive well before the 4:30 p.m. cutoff.

Vital records live at this counter too, and some come up during a home sale. Heirs may need a death certificate, a marriage record can affect who signs, and notaries book by appointment.

  • Certified birth, death and marriage certificates: $10 each, with requests directed through the county's vital records portal.
  • Marriage license: $60.
  • Notary appointment: $10 each.
  • Copies of any record: $0.10 apiece.

If heirs need a certified certificate, order it early so the title company has it when the file is reviewed.

sections.h2: Questions to settle before closing day
sections.html:
A short call to the right office can save a delay. Ring the register at 828-837-2613 to check the fee for your page count and ask about any plat. Phone the Appraisal Office at 828-835-3296 if the parcel record does not look right or if you receive tax relief. Then have your attorney tell you the stamp amount that will print on the settlement statement.

Doing this a week ahead leaves time to correct a missing owner, an old lien or a plat problem. The register records what you hand over and does not review it for mistakes.

Paying cash does not move the deed around the recorder. It still goes through the Murphy counter, the stamp still applies, and any deed of trust on your side still needs a payoff and a recorded release. What a cash sale removes is the buyer's appraisal and underwriting wait, which is often where inherited or repair-heavy houses stall. You still choose the closing attorney, the deed still has to match your vesting deed, and the Murphy office still files it at the same price per page.

Deal with the tax bill, the loan payoff and title questions before the attorney files. Property tax comes due September 1, and interest starts January 6, as set by G.S. 105-360. Because the lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, closing usually pays the current bill out of the proceeds.

Four steps keep a sale moving.

  • Identify every owner in the chain of title, including heirs on an inherited house.
  • Where lot lines are unclear, a surveyor can advise on plats, which are a separate $21 filing.
  • Request a payoff letter from each lender. Recording the release is free.
  • Dig out your vesting deed so the new deed repeats its legal description exactly.

Staff record documents but never write them, so a North Carolina attorney should prepare the deed. When repairs, liens or squabbling heirs have stalled a sale, a cash purchase avoids a lender's timetable. Our North Carolina page explains that route.

faqs.q: Where is the Cherokee County register's office?
faqs.a: 75 Peachtree Street, Suite 126-A, Murphy, NC 28906. Call 828-837-2613, and bring land records in by 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What does recording a Cherokee County deed cost?
faqs.a: A deed up to 15 pages is $26, then $4 a page. Deeds of trust are $64 up to 35 pages, and a plat filing is $21.

faqs.q: How are Cherokee County deed stamps figured?
faqs.a: At $2 for each $1,000 of price, the same rate the state writes as $1.00 per $500. The seller pays it when the deed goes on record.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about a Cherokee County tax value?
faqs.a: The Cherokee County Appraisal Office, at 828-835-3296, handles questions about parcel data and values.

faqs.q: Is there a charge for deed copies?
faqs.a: Yes. Plain copies are ten cents a page. A certified document is $5 for page one and $2 per page afterward, and vital record certificates are $10 each.
